How to Style Woven Baskets in Every Room of the Home

A styling guide, not a tutorial: where to place woven baskets, what size to choose for each room, and the two rules that stop them looking cluttered.

22 January 2026 ME By Maya Ellis 9 min read 583 words
Share

On this page

  1. The two rules that matter most
  2. Which size for which room
  3. Placement ideas that always work

In short

A styling guide, not a tutorial: where to place woven baskets, what size to choose for each room, and the two rules that stop them looking cluttered.

Most people own a woven basket and still feel their room looks unfinished. The problem is rarely the basket; it is that baskets are treated as storage rather than as design. This is a styling guide, so there is no weaving here, just the placement and sizing decisions that make natural pieces look intentional.

Two rules do most of the work. First, a basket should be large enough to look deliberate in the space it occupies. Second, baskets work in odd-numbered groups of different sizes, never as a matching set. Everything below follows from those two ideas.

The reason a lone small basket disappears is scale. A 20 cm basket on a wide shelf or beside a deep sofa reads as clutter, while the same basket on a narrow windowsill looks considered. Before you buy or place anything, measure the surface it will sit on and aim for a basket that fills roughly a third of that width. That single proportion fixes more styling problems than any other change.

The two rules that matter most

Rule one is scale: choose a basket that fills about a third of the surface it sits on. Rule two is grouping: arrange three baskets of different heights, in odd numbers, rather than two identical ones. A pair looks like a mistake; a trio looks styled. Keep the tallest in the middle or at one end, never dead centre in a symmetrical row.

  • Fill about a third of the surface with the largest basket.
  • Group in odd numbers, three is easiest.
  • Vary the heights by at least 8 cm between pieces.
  • Leave one basket empty so the group can breathe.
  • Keep the colour of the group within one family: natural, honey or deep brown.

Which size for which room

Sizes are not interchangeable between rooms, because the scale of the furniture changes. A basket that looks generous in a hallway looks tiny next to a sofa. The table below is the sizing I use and recommend, measured across the widest point of the basket.

RoomIdeal sizeBest use
Living room40 to 50 cmBlankets beside the sofa
Bedroom30 to 40 cmLaundry or spare throws
Kitchen25 to 30 cmBread, fruit or utensils
Bathroom20 to 25 cmRolled towels or toiletries
Hallway45 to 55 cmShoes, bags and umbrellas
Shelf or console18 to 22 cmGrouped as a trio with plants

Placement ideas that always work

Some placements are dependable because they answer a real need rather than decorating for its own sake. A basket beside the sofa catches blankets; one by the door catches shoes. When a basket has a job, it never looks like clutter, and that is the whole secret of styling with natural pieces.

Try a large floor basket with a rolled throw and one flat cushion on top, a medium basket on a shelf holding a plant, and a small one on a side table for the television remotes. Three rooms, three jobs, one material, and the whole home feels more settled.

Helpful Tips

  • Keep the largest basket on the floor, never on a shelf, unless it is under 25 cm.
  • Put a rolled textile in at least one basket so it reads as intended, not empty.
  • Line a kitchen basket with a linen cloth to stop crumbs falling through the weave.
  • Rotate the baskets between rooms each season so the styling feels fresh without buying anything.

Frequently asked questions

How many woven baskets should I group together?

Group in odd numbers, usually three. Use different heights, at least 8 cm apart, and keep them within one colour family so the group looks styled rather than accidental.

What size basket should go beside a sofa?

For a living room, a 40 to 50 cm basket measured across the widest point. Anything under 30 cm disappears next to a deep sofa and reads as clutter.

Should baskets be empty or full?

Leave at least one in a group empty so the arrangement can breathe, and fill the largest with a rolled throw or cushion so it clearly has a purpose.

Can I use woven baskets in a bathroom?

Yes, a 20 to 25 cm basket works well for rolled towels or toiletries. Keep it away from direct splashes and dry it if it gets damp, since damp shortens the life of the weave.
